entities.title: Fall of the Old Keep
entities.summary: The Old Keep falls in a single night to a shadow that came down from the high passes.
entities.body:
On the third night of Longnight, 612 AS, the watchfires of the [[The Old Keep|Old Keep]]
went dark. Riders from [[Raven's Vale]] found the gates open and the courtyards
empty by morning. Whatever passed that night left no bodies, only frost.

The keep has stood abandoned ever since.

entities.title: Founding of Thornhold
entities.summary: Lord Garron raises the red walls of Thornhold above the iron veins of the Spinegrey range.
entities.body:
Forty-seven years after the [[The Sundering|Sundering]], settlers from the eastern
ports broke the first stones of [[Thornhold]] from the cliffside. The
foundation feast lasted nine days, ending with the lighting of the Forge of
Garron — still tended today.

entities.title: The Sundering
entities.summary: The cataclysm that split the old continent and ended the Third Age. The new calendar reckons years from the day the sky cracked.
entities.body:
When the Twin Moons collided in the night sky, the firmament tore and the seas
boiled. Half of the old continent slid beneath the waves; what remained
became the Astrath Deeprealm. Survivors founded the great cities of
[[Thornhold]] and [[Sunhaven]] in the years that followed.

This event marks year **0** of the *After Sundering* calendar.

entities.title: Corven
entities.summary: Legendary Tidemarrow underworld figure whose name and face have become tools for smugglers, proxies, and liars.
entities.body:
# Corven
*A smuggler-king of the [[02_Regions/Tidemarrow]] underworld, whose face is on a hundred wanted posters and a hundred liars.*

A legendary [[Underground]] figure whose name is woven into half the great heists of the past decades. He has not been seen in years, but his name still opens doors. Crews invoke him to recruit, to threaten, to close a deal. So many people have worn his face that the legend is no longer entirely under his control, if it ever was.

![[Corven.webp]]

## Appearance

The stories agree on the shape of him: tall and wiry, late thirties to early forties, ash-blond hair parted right with a small cowlick at the crown. Clear blue eyes. Sharp cheekbones, defined jaw, thin nose, gentled by a faint mouth and a relaxed brow. A nick through the left eyebrow. He is most often described in a river-grey long coat with hidden pockets, the hem hanging unnaturally straight, and a signet ring set with a chipped dark stone. Faint scent of fennel and cedar.

Wanted posters and tavern stories have repeated these details so often that nobody is certain which were ever real. Most who claim to have met him also describe a calm voice, a slight smile, and the kind of stillness in a room that reads as confidence rather than caution.

## Rumors and Legends

Some say he never failed a heist that he himself led. Others say half the heists credited to him were never his work, only his name flown like a flag.

He has not been seen in years. Younger crews have begun insisting he is dead. Older ones laugh at younger crews. There are smugglers who claim he hand-picks proxies and hires them out, that the men robbing vaults under his name are paid impersonators and he is the silent partner. There are smugglers who claim he is plotting something none of his proxies could match, in some cellar in [[02_Regions/Tidemarrow]] no one has the eye for. There are smugglers who refuse to speak of him at all, which is a different kind of answer.

Nobody agrees on which is the truth, and the doubt itself is now part of the legend.

%%
## DM Notes

### Truth (unresolved)

Three live possibilities, none committed:

1. **Alive, lying low.** He let the legend run while he stepped back. Plotting something larger, more patient, harder to trace.
2. **Alive, running proxies.** Several impersonators are sanctioned, paid, fed instructions. The real Corven directs from somewhere safer.
3. **Dead.** The legend kept walking on its own momentum. Imposters multiplied without anyone left to disagree.

The party will encounter convincing fakes long before they encounter anything resembling truth. Pick a possibility when the campaign forces a commitment, not before.

### At-table cues

- **Voice:** calm, low, unhurried. He never raises it because he never needs to.
- **Mannerism:** charismatic, bold, overconfident, scheming. The composure is a performance of confidence, not its absence.
- **Tells:** two-finger tap on the table before a deal. Pause before naming a number. Looks at hands first, then eyes.
- **Body:** relaxed posture, slight smile.

### Real-vs-fake tells

When the party needs to test whether the Corven in front of them is the man, a sanctioned proxy, or a chancer wearing the face:

- **Onyx signet:** real piece is dark stone with a tiny star nick on the left edge. Most fakes use painted brass.
- **Coat hem:** real Corven's coat (or his Engineering robe variant) has hand-sewn hem weights used by field surveyors, not classroom cuts.
- **Coat condition:** real Corven keeps it clean. Fakes let the cloth take ore dust that refracts near a lamp.
- **Gait:** the real man's right foot angles a touch outward. Many imposters over-stride trying to look confident.
- **Scent:** fennel and cedar, faint. Most fakes don't bother.

### Mask recipe (used by Shifters and proxies)

Ash-blond wig parted right. Leather half-mask to sharpen the jaw. Blue glass bead pinned inside the collar to brighten eye color under lamplight. Weighted coat hem. Brass signet copy. The surface manner (calm voice, two-finger tap, pause before numbers) practiced as table behavior.

### Plot hooks

- Any encounter with "Corven" is a question, not an answer. Who is this person, who hired them, what do they actually know about the real man.
- If alive, the real Corven reacts to public uses of his name. A crew that abuses the legend may attract a quiet correction.
- Whoever runs the proxies (if option 2) is the actual power behind the legend. That figure is not yet decided.

### Appearances
*To be filled as he or his name surfaces in sessions.*
%%

entities.title: Edric
entities.summary: Harwick's Vein-Marked companion, riding ahead toward Stavall after the Ashbrook Manor sequence.
entities.body:
# Edric
*Harwick's old companion, riding hard for Stavall.*

Edric was the [[Vein-Marked]] companion of [[Harwick]], the previous owner of [[Ashbrook Manor]]. After the Ashbrook sequence, he rode ahead of the party toward [[Stavall]], setting a hard pace that suggests he knows where he is going.


![[Edric.webp]]
## Appearance
Edric is lean and windburned, with sandy hair tied back, tired sharp eyes, and faint blue vein-marks running up one side of his neck.

%%
## DM Notes

### Truth

Edric is a chase target, not yet a confrontation. The party is racing him to Stavall. He may be carrying intelligence the facility wants, fleeing toward the only people who would shelter him, or both. He may be heading for the same facility as Mars.

The [[Wakewall Gate]]'s civilian clerk's ledger gives the party the chance to confirm whether he reached the city, when, and under what name. [[Thresh]] reads the gate ledger by evening; he may notice Edric before the party does.

### Plot hooks

- The party can catch him on the road, intercept him at the gate, or arrive too late and find him already inside the facility.
- His relationship to Harwick is the throughline. Was he Harwick's protector, his betrayer, or his fellow believer?

### Appearances
- [[Campaign Synthesis and story archs]]
- [[Session 10]]
%%

entities.title: Soreth
entities.body:
**Full Title:** Soreth, The Crown (formerly), The Fallen One (current)  
**Role:** Hierarchy Enforcer (formerly), Corrupted Runner (current)  
**Type:** [[Sarim]] (Entropic, running wild)  
**Organization:** Opposes [[Sarim|The Sarim]]  
**Status:** Permanently corrupted, leads legions, believes righteous

---

_What was made to bind has come undone._

Soreth was once called the Crown, an enforcer of order among [[Sarim]], chosen again and again to bear Entropy because their strength never wavered. They believed endurance proved worth. That holding the burden longer made them greater. When others broke, Soreth stood strong.

They bore the burden far past what was safe. Not out of duty, but pride. And when the burden became too much, they did not fall. They rose, warped, convinced, burning with purpose.

They returned home as something new. Not broken. Not lost. Transformed. They killed [[Nepheth]], the keeper of return. They shattered [[Nepheth|Nepheth's]] [[Anchors|Anchor]] and destroyed their Scales so no call would bring them back. Then they left. No redemption. No final word.

Soreth has not stopped moving since.

They gather legions. They preach strength as salvation and call corruption a trial to be mastered. To mortals, they may seem radiant. To [[Gods]], persuasive. To their siblings, unrecognizable.

And yet they were one of the Thirteen Sarim. They were trusted. Cared for.

Still wearing the Crown. Still believing they are right.

Their [[Anchors|Anchor]] remains.

_If they fall, they may return. If the [[Anchors|Anchor]] breaks, they are gone forever. [[Sarim|The Sarim]] wait, blade half-drawn._

---

## Known Actions & Reputation

**What the world knows:**

- Leads forces across multiple planes
- Commands strange, silent legions of "perfected" beings
- Preaches that strength and endurance prove worth
- Claims the Sarim's preservation stifles necessary growth
- Has evaded pursuit for centuries
- Soreth is the creator of [[The Absolved]], purified entropic creatures like [[Scar-Spawn]], shaped into orderly beings.

**Common rhetoric attributed to Soreth:**

> "The weak cling to return. The strong do not need it."

> "I preserve through strength, not obedience."

> "The system is broken. I will not let truth be forgotten."

**What the Sarim say:**

- Once one of the most trusted
- Bore Entropy longer than any other to prove their strength
- Something changed in them during Ezareth's absence
- Killed Nepheth to "break a broken system"
- The Resilient speak of Soreth as their greatest fear

---

%%DM NOTE: EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS DM-ONLY INFORMATION%%

%%

## The Fall - Complete Timeline

### Their Enduring Test (Years 2,080-2,155, 75 years)

Unlike the other Sarim, Soreth held Entropy for longer, enough to experience it directly. They learned its signature, its feeling, its nature. And in learning this, they developed a sensitivity no other Sarim possessed: they could separate Entropy's unending, overwriting madness from its magical potential.

It allowed them a new sight - to distinguish Entropy from natural creation through [[Path of Creation]].

**Key Development:**

- Learned to feel the difference between Entropy corruption and divine creation
- Believed this made them more effective hunters
- Saw themselves as mastering the burden others merely endured
- Pride disguised as dedication

### The Revelation (Years 2,135-2,155, ~20 years)

Soreth began to notice a pattern. Every god they hunted was using [[Path of Creation]]. Not spreading Entropy. Not corrupting mortals. Just creating. Making new races, new things, exercising divine prerogative.

Soreth tested their senses repeatedly. "This new race doesn't carry the Entropy signature. It's just... growth. Just creation."

**The truth crystallized, clear and terrible:**

- The Sarim were not hunting corruption
- They were hunting creation itself
- Gods were being destroyed for exercising their fundamental nature
- Growth was being stifled under the guise of preservation

### The Rejection (Years 2,155-2,165, ~10 years)

Soreth brought their findings to [[The Sovereign Eternal|Ezareth]]. Presented evidence. Demonstrated the distinction between Entropy and natural creation.

**Ezareth's response:** "You have held corruption too long. Your judgment is compromised. Return to rotation."

**The ultimate wound:**

- The one Sarim who could tell the difference was the one whose testimony couldn't be trusted
- Soreth's unique qualification was their disqualification
- Fear: "When I die and reforge, this truth dies with me. The system will continue unchanged."
- No one else could distinguish creation from corruption
- If Soreth let go now, nothing would change

### The Corruption (Years 2,165-2,200, 35 years)

Soreth refused to release the burden. They would not forget. They would not let the truth be lost.

But Entropy does not wait for noble intentions. The Stage 3 corruption they carried for so long began to twist everything. The truth they had seen clearly became justification for increasingly corrupted methods.

**Logic shift by Year 2,180:**

- The system is broken (true insight)
- Therefore, I must break the system (corrupted conclusion)
- Nepheth's cycle perpetuates the dogma (true observation)
- Therefore, I must kill Nepheth (corrupted solution)

**Final acceleration (Years 2,197-2,200):**

- Ezareth left for three years (legitimate emergency)
- Soreth bore triple burden alone
- Final push into absolute certainty
- Point of no return crossed

### The Murder (Year 2,200)

Soreth killed [[Nepheth]]. Shattered their sibling's [[Anchors|Anchor]]. Destroyed the Scales—ground them to powder and scattered the pieces to places Sarim could not easily reach.

**Soreth's belief:** They were liberating the system  
**Reality:** They had broken it permanently

They fled. They gathered legions. And even now, eight hundred and eighteen years later, leading corrupted forces across the planes, Soreth believes they are righteous.

They are the only one who saw the truth.  
They are also the only one who is irredeemably lost.

---

## Current State - Full Details

### Physical Appearance

Soreth still wears the Crown.

This is perhaps the most tragic element of their corruption. While other Stage 3 Entropic become visibly twisted, Soreth remains _recognizably themselves_. The Crown still sits geometric and gold (perhaps slightly darkened) upon their head. They retain the same number of arms, the same eye pattern, the same general silhouette.

The corruption lives in their eyes, their words, their absolute certainty—not in their form.

**Visual Markers:**

- **Crown:** Geometric gold, slightly darker/tarnished than before
- **Eyes:** Seven golden eyes in perfect circle, but the focus is _wrong_
- **Arms:** Six arms, same as always, but movements more precise, rigid
- **Wings:** Two black wings, perhaps with more geometric order to feathers
- **Tentacles:** Black with golden script, but patterns more angular
- **Armor:** Bronze and obsidian, unchanged from before

**To other Sarim:**

- Corruption obvious in how Soreth _moves_ and _speaks_
- Terrible certainty, rigid precision
- Inability to see themselves clearly

**To Soreth:**

- Looks exactly as they always did
- Proof they haven't fallen
- Proof they've simply _understood_ what others refuse to see

### The Crown's Second Function

Soreth has discovered—or believes they've discovered—the Crown's "true purpose."

The Crown can command living beings (its original function). But Soreth has learned it can also _perfect_ corrupted beings. By channeling their Stage 3 Entropy through the Crown's authority structure, they can transform screaming Scar-spawn into silent, obedient formations of geometric perfection.

They call this "absolution."

**The Process:**

1. Soreth approaches Entropic (Stage 1-2 Scar-spawn, corrupted entities)
2. The Crown pulses with cold, precise light
3. Authority flows from Crown into the corrupted form
4. Chaos solidifies into geometric perfection
5. What remains is silent, obedient, "purified"

**The Result: The Absolved**

- Entropic entities transformed into rigid, crystalline formations
- Move in perfect synchronization
- No screaming, no chaos, only silent purpose
- Arranged in geometric patterns
- Utterly obedient to Soreth's will
- The Absolved do not just look like crystals; they look like crude, forced imitations of  the Sarim. Soreth is trying to build a family out of monsters.

**Soreth's belief:**

> "This is what the Crown was always meant to do. Not command through voice, but through _correction_. I have not fallen. I have finally understood."

---

## Mechanics & Combat

### Power Level

- **CR 22-25** on [[Mortal Plane]] (weakened by plane's "heaviness")
- **CR 26-28** on other planes
- Stage 3 Entropy amplification makes them stronger than uncorrupted Sarim
- Commands The Absolved (CR 5-15 typically, hundreds of them)

### Tactics

- **Infiltration:** May initially appear helpful/uncorrupted
- **Persuasion:** Preaches strength-as-salvation to recruits
- **Command:** Uses The Absolved as disciplined legions
- **Strategic:** Leads incursions against Anchors, divine strongholds
- **Opportunistic:** Targets weakened gods, corrupted regions
- **Patient:** Has evaded pursuit for 818 years, will not fight to death

### Combat Notes

- Uses Sarim tactics: precise, overwhelming, surgical
- Knows weaknesses of each Sarim (and possibly the party's)
- Can flee to other planes if overwhelmed
- Will retreat if fight turns—too important for the "work"
- Commands hundreds of The Absolved as reinforcements

### Armies & Assets

- **The Absolved:** Hundreds of "purified" Entropic entities
- **Corrupted followers:** Some mortals/gods drawn to rhetoric
- **Unknowing allies:** Some may not realize corruption
- **Strategic assets:** Controls regions within The Scar, outposts on multiple planes

---

## The Anchor Dilemma

### The Situation

Soreth's [[Anchors|Anchor]] remains intact in the Sarim home chamber, guarded by [[Ezareth]].

**If Soreth dies and the Crown is recovered:**

- Could reforge in approximately **250 years** (current degraded system: 8 years × 30 due to massive Stage 3 Entropy corruption)
- **Without the Crown:** Would take ~2,500 years minimum (10x multiplier)

### The Philosophical Split

**Redemptionists** (preserve Anchor):

- Soreth was corrupted, not inherently evil
- They held the burden too long _for us_
- They saw truth we refused to acknowledge
- 250 years to potentially return clean
- Destroying Anchor = giving up on them forever
- What if they remember the truth when they return?

**Eliminationists** (destroy Anchor):

- Every day Soreth runs free, more damage done
- Stage 3 corruption may be permanent (reforging unproven at this level)
- Destroyed Nepheth's chance at return—showed no mercy
- Cannot risk them returning with memories intact
- Some sins are unforgivable
- System can't survive waiting 250 years

### Ezareth's Position

[[Ezareth]] has guarded the Anchor for 818 years. Has not destroyed it. Has not spoken publicly about which position they hold.

**Internal conflict:**

- Must choose between permanent loss and long-shot return
- Every passing day brings more damage
- Guilt: "I should have stayed. I should have seen."
- Hope: "They were corrupted, not evil. 250 years... maybe..."
- Pragmatism: "How many more will die while we wait?"

**Quote:**

> "You were my strongest. That's why you fell. That's why I failed you. That's why I stand here still, waiting to see if I was right to hope."

---

## Relationships

### [[Ezareth|The Sovereign Eternal]]

- Parental trust turned to burden and guilt
- Hunts Soreth personally when they draw near home
- Torn between grief and resolve
- Guards the Anchor but hasn't destroyed it
- "I should have stayed. I should have seen."
- Feels responsible for leaving during critical 3 years

### [[Kadesh]] & The Resilient

- Soreth is their nightmare—proof bearing Entropy corrupts absolutely
- Their rotation now defined by _not becoming Soreth_
- Often say: "Kill me before I turn."
- Kadesh especially haunted (killed Soreth once, thought he'd saved him)
- Fear: "If Soreth fell, any of us could"

### The Other Sarim

- Pity and horror mixed
- Split between redemption and elimination
- Some see Soreth's truth (the system _is_ broken)
- Some see only the corruption
- All agree: cannot let them destroy more Anchors
- Creates paranoia: "Can we trust our own judgment about bearing Entropy?"

### [[Nepheth]]

- First to die permanently
- Strategic target (Nepheth maintained the cycle)
- Symbolic target (break the system to free it)
- Personal element (Nepheth rejected Soreth's testimony)
- Unclear whether Soreth even remembers why they chose Nepheth first
- May have been corrupted logic: "Kill the maintainer, expose the flaw"

---

## Threat Assessment

### Immediate Dangers

- Leads incursions against Primordial Anchors
- Converts Entropic into The Absolved (growing army)
- May infiltrate as ally to gather intelligence
- Hunts current Sarim (especially The Resilient)
- Spreads Stage 3 Entropy through [[Path of Transference]]
- Philosophically persuasive (some points are _true_)

### Strategic Threats

- Former insider: knows all Sarim structures, weaknesses, locations
- May have knowledge of Anchor destruction techniques
- Could destroy remaining Anchors, making all Sarim deaths permanent
- Creates paranoia within Sarim: "If the strongest fell, who's next?"
- Philosophically dangerous: his critique of the system resonates
- Time is on his side: every year degrades the system further

### Long-term Implications

- Proof that bearing Entropy permanently corrupts (supports rigidity)
- Evidence that system itself may be flawed (supports reform)
- Question: Can preservation coexist with growth?
- Problem: If he's right about creation vs. corruption, what does that mean for Sarim purpose?
- Redemptionist/Eliminationist split may tear Sarim apart from within

---

## For Players

### Encounter Framework

**First Encounter (Possible Deception):**

- May appear as helpful Sarim, aligned with players
- Offers assistance against common threat
- Subtle wrongness in behavior, "off" feeling
- Rhetoric about strength, endurance, broken systems
- Insight DC 25+ to detect (20+ if familiar with Sarim lore)

**Second Encounter (Growing Suspicion):**

- Inconsistencies emerge in knowledge or methods
- NPCs or other Sarim express concern
- Players may witness The Absolved in action
- Pattern of "perfecting" rather than destroying corruption
- Geometric precision feels wrong for preservation-focused being

**Final Confrontation:**

- Still believes they are righteous
- May offer players philosophical choice: "Join me in breaking a broken system"
- Commands The Absolved against party
- Will retreat if fight turns badly (patient, strategic, has long game)
- May leave prophetic warning: "You'll see. When you bear it long enough, you'll understand."

### Player Choices

**If Players Discover the Anchor:**

- **Destroy it:** Permanent death, eliminationist position, pragmatic
- **Guard it:** Preserve chance of return, redemptionist position, hopeful
- **Conceal it:** Delay the choice, kick can down road, political

**If Players Capture the Crown:**

- **Return to Ezareth:** Enable potential reforging (250 years)
- **Destroy it:** Extend reforging to 2,500+ years (near-permanent)
- **Keep it:** Wield legendary power, slowly die/transform
- **Hide it:** Prevent reforging entirely, deny Sarim the choice

**If Players Hear His Rhetoric:**

- He's not entirely wrong about the system being rigid
- His methods are absolutely monstrous
- Creates philosophical question: reform vs. rebellion
- No easy answers—players must decide what they believe

**Crown as Item (if recovered):**

- Provides immense power (CR boost, command abilities, create Absolved)
- Slowly transforms/corrupts wielder (geometric thinking, rigid certainty)
- Enable Soreth's eventual reforging if returned to Anchor
- Impossible for most mortals to wield without dying
- Soreth's Echo may influence wielder

---

## The Tragedy (DM Thematic Notes)

**What makes Soreth tragic:**

**Soreth was right:**

- The Sarim _were_ hunting creation, not just corruption
- The system _was_ rigid
- Growth _was_ being stifled under preservation
- They had genuine insight no other Sarim possessed

**Soreth is corrupted:**

- Methods are monstrous (murder, destruction, enslavement)
- Certainty is absolute delusion
- "Absolution" is corruption wearing mask of salvation
- Cannot see how far they've fallen

**The deeper questions:**

1. Was it the corruption that made Soreth break the system?
2. Or was it the system that made Soreth keep corruption until it broke them?
3. If they return in 250 years, reforged clean, will they remember the truth?
4. If they remember, will they fall again? Was the fall inevitable?
5. What defines failure: breaking under burden, or refusing to break?

**The irony:**

- Soreth is proof of Sarim dogma: "See? Even the one who tried to understand growth became corrupted. This is why we preserve, not adapt."
- But deeper irony: It was Sarim rigidity and rejection that contributed to the fall
- Had they listened when Soreth was still clear, perhaps things would have been different
- Both sides can claim vindication; neither can claim innocence

**For your table:**

- No easy answers—players must grapple with complexity
- Some sins may be unforgivable; some systems may be irredeemable

- Corruption can wear the face of righteousness

entities.bodyHtml:
Full Title: Soreth, The Crown (formerly), The Fallen One (current)
Role: Hierarchy Enforcer (formerly), Corrupted Runner (current)
Type: Sarim (Entropic, running wild)
Organization: Opposes The Sarim
Status: Permanently corrupted, leads legions, believes righteous

What was made to bind has come undone.

Soreth was once called the Crown, an enforcer of order among Sarim, chosen again and again to bear Entropy because their strength never wavered. They believed endurance proved worth. That holding the burden longer made them greater. When others broke, Soreth stood strong.

They bore the burden far past what was safe. Not out of duty, but pride. And when the burden became too much, they did not fall. They rose, warped, convinced, burning with purpose.

They returned home as something new. Not broken. Not lost. Transformed. They killed Nepheth, the keeper of return. They shattered Nepheth's Anchor and destroyed their Scales so no call would bring them back. Then they left. No redemption. No final word.

Soreth has not stopped moving since.

They gather legions. They preach strength as salvation and call corruption a trial to be mastered. To mortals, they may seem radiant. To Gods, persuasive. To their siblings, unrecognizable.

And yet they were one of the Thirteen Sarim. They were trusted. Cared for.

Still wearing the Crown. Still believing they are right.

Their Anchor remains.

If they fall, they may return. If the Anchor breaks, they are gone forever. The Sarim wait, blade half-drawn.

Known Actions & Reputation

What the world knows:

  • Leads forces across multiple planes
  • Commands strange, silent legions of "perfected" beings
  • Preaches that strength and endurance prove worth
  • Claims the Sarim's preservation stifles necessary growth
  • Has evaded pursuit for centuries
  • Soreth is the creator of The Absolved, purified entropic creatures like Scar-Spawn, shaped into orderly beings.

Common rhetoric attributed to Soreth:

"The weak cling to return. The strong do not need it."

"I preserve through strength, not obedience."

"The system is broken. I will not let truth be forgotten."

What the Sarim say:

  • Once one of the most trusted
  • Bore Entropy longer than any other to prove their strength
  • Something changed in them during Ezareth's absence
  • Killed Nepheth to "break a broken system"
  • The Resilient speak of Soreth as their greatest fear

%%DM NOTE: EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS DM-ONLY INFORMATION%%

%%

The Fall - Complete Timeline

Their Enduring Test (Years 2,080-2,155, 75 years)

Unlike the other Sarim, Soreth held Entropy for longer, enough to experience it directly. They learned its signature, its feeling, its nature. And in learning this, they developed a sensitivity no other Sarim possessed: they could separate Entropy's unending, overwriting madness from its magical potential.

It allowed them a new sight - to distinguish Entropy from natural creation through Path of Creation.

Key Development:

  • Learned to feel the difference between Entropy corruption and divine creation
  • Believed this made them more effective hunters
  • Saw themselves as mastering the burden others merely endured
  • Pride disguised as dedication

The Revelation (Years 2,135-2,155, ~20 years)

Soreth began to notice a pattern. Every god they hunted was using Path of Creation. Not spreading Entropy. Not corrupting mortals. Just creating. Making new races, new things, exercising divine prerogative.

Soreth tested their senses repeatedly. "This new race doesn't carry the Entropy signature. It's just... growth. Just creation."

The truth crystallized, clear and terrible:

  • The Sarim were not hunting corruption
  • They were hunting creation itself
  • Gods were being destroyed for exercising their fundamental nature
  • Growth was being stifled under the guise of preservation

The Rejection (Years 2,155-2,165, ~10 years)

Soreth brought their findings to Ezareth. Presented evidence. Demonstrated the distinction between Entropy and natural creation.

Ezareth's response: "You have held corruption too long. Your judgment is compromised. Return to rotation."

The ultimate wound:

  • The one Sarim who could tell the difference was the one whose testimony couldn't be trusted
  • Soreth's unique qualification was their disqualification
  • Fear: "When I die and reforge, this truth dies with me. The system will continue unchanged."
  • No one else could distinguish creation from corruption
  • If Soreth let go now, nothing would change

The Corruption (Years 2,165-2,200, 35 years)

Soreth refused to release the burden. They would not forget. They would not let the truth be lost.

But Entropy does not wait for noble intentions. The Stage 3 corruption they carried for so long began to twist everything. The truth they had seen clearly became justification for increasingly corrupted methods.

Logic shift by Year 2,180:

  • The system is broken (true insight)
  • Therefore, I must break the system (corrupted conclusion)
  • Nepheth's cycle perpetuates the dogma (true observation)
  • Therefore, I must kill Nepheth (corrupted solution)

Final acceleration (Years 2,197-2,200):

  • Ezareth left for three years (legitimate emergency)
  • Soreth bore triple burden alone
  • Final push into absolute certainty
  • Point of no return crossed

The Murder (Year 2,200)

Soreth killed Nepheth. Shattered their sibling's Anchor. Destroyed the Scales—ground them to powder and scattered the pieces to places Sarim could not easily reach.

Soreth's belief: They were liberating the system
Reality: They had broken it permanently

They fled. They gathered legions. And even now, eight hundred and eighteen years later, leading corrupted forces across the planes, Soreth believes they are righteous.

They are the only one who saw the truth.
They are also the only one who is irredeemably lost.

Current State - Full Details

Physical Appearance

Soreth still wears the Crown.

This is perhaps the most tragic element of their corruption. While other Stage 3 Entropic become visibly twisted, Soreth remains recognizably themselves. The Crown still sits geometric and gold (perhaps slightly darkened) upon their head. They retain the same number of arms, the same eye pattern, the same general silhouette.

The corruption lives in their eyes, their words, their absolute certainty—not in their form.

Visual Markers:

  • Crown: Geometric gold, slightly darker/tarnished than before
  • Eyes: Seven golden eyes in perfect circle, but the focus is wrong
  • Arms: Six arms, same as always, but movements more precise, rigid
  • Wings: Two black wings, perhaps with more geometric order to feathers
  • Tentacles: Black with golden script, but patterns more angular
  • Armor: Bronze and obsidian, unchanged from before

To other Sarim:

  • Corruption obvious in how Soreth moves and speaks
  • Terrible certainty, rigid precision
  • Inability to see themselves clearly

To Soreth:

  • Looks exactly as they always did
  • Proof they haven't fallen
  • Proof they've simply understood what others refuse to see

The Crown's Second Function

Soreth has discovered—or believes they've discovered—the Crown's "true purpose."

The Crown can command living beings (its original function). But Soreth has learned it can also perfect corrupted beings. By channeling their Stage 3 Entropy through the Crown's authority structure, they can transform screaming Scar-spawn into silent, obedient formations of geometric perfection.

They call this "absolution."

The Process:

  1. Soreth approaches Entropic (Stage 1-2 Scar-spawn, corrupted entities)
  2. The Crown pulses with cold, precise light
  3. Authority flows from Crown into the corrupted form
  4. Chaos solidifies into geometric perfection
  5. What remains is silent, obedient, "purified"

The Result: The Absolved

  • Entropic entities transformed into rigid, crystalline formations
  • Move in perfect synchronization
  • No screaming, no chaos, only silent purpose
  • Arranged in geometric patterns
  • Utterly obedient to Soreth's will
  • The Absolved do not just look like crystals; they look like crude, forced imitations of the Sarim. Soreth is trying to build a family out of monsters.

Soreth's belief:

"This is what the Crown was always meant to do. Not command through voice, but through correction. I have not fallen. I have finally understood."

Mechanics & Combat

Power Level

  • CR 22-25 on Mortal Plane (weakened by plane's "heaviness")
  • CR 26-28 on other planes
  • Stage 3 Entropy amplification makes them stronger than uncorrupted Sarim
  • Commands The Absolved (CR 5-15 typically, hundreds of them)

Tactics

  • Infiltration: May initially appear helpful/uncorrupted
  • Persuasion: Preaches strength-as-salvation to recruits
  • Command: Uses The Absolved as disciplined legions
  • Strategic: Leads incursions against Anchors, divine strongholds
  • Opportunistic: Targets weakened gods, corrupted regions
  • Patient: Has evaded pursuit for 818 years, will not fight to death

Combat Notes

  • Uses Sarim tactics: precise, overwhelming, surgical
  • Knows weaknesses of each Sarim (and possibly the party's)
  • Can flee to other planes if overwhelmed
  • Will retreat if fight turns—too important for the "work"
  • Commands hundreds of The Absolved as reinforcements

Armies & Assets

  • The Absolved: Hundreds of "purified" Entropic entities
  • Corrupted followers: Some mortals/gods drawn to rhetoric
  • Unknowing allies: Some may not realize corruption
  • Strategic assets: Controls regions within The Scar, outposts on multiple planes

The Anchor Dilemma

The Situation

Soreth's Anchor remains intact in the Sarim home chamber, guarded by Ezareth.

If Soreth dies and the Crown is recovered:

  • Could reforge in approximately 250 years (current degraded system: 8 years × 30 due to massive Stage 3 Entropy corruption)
  • Without the Crown: Would take ~2,500 years minimum (10x multiplier)

The Philosophical Split

Redemptionists (preserve Anchor):

  • Soreth was corrupted, not inherently evil
  • They held the burden too long for us
  • They saw truth we refused to acknowledge
  • 250 years to potentially return clean
  • Destroying Anchor = giving up on them forever
  • What if they remember the truth when they return?

Eliminationists (destroy Anchor):

  • Every day Soreth runs free, more damage done
  • Stage 3 corruption may be permanent (reforging unproven at this level)
  • Destroyed Nepheth's chance at return—showed no mercy
  • Cannot risk them returning with memories intact
  • Some sins are unforgivable
  • System can't survive waiting 250 years

Ezareth's Position

Ezareth has guarded the Anchor for 818 years. Has not destroyed it. Has not spoken publicly about which position they hold.

Internal conflict:

  • Must choose between permanent loss and long-shot return
  • Every passing day brings more damage
  • Guilt: "I should have stayed. I should have seen."
  • Hope: "They were corrupted, not evil. 250 years... maybe..."
  • Pragmatism: "How many more will die while we wait?"

Quote:

"You were my strongest. That's why you fell. That's why I failed you. That's why I stand here still, waiting to see if I was right to hope."

Relationships

The Sovereign Eternal

  • Parental trust turned to burden and guilt
  • Hunts Soreth personally when they draw near home
  • Torn between grief and resolve
  • Guards the Anchor but hasn't destroyed it
  • "I should have stayed. I should have seen."
  • Feels responsible for leaving during critical 3 years

Kadesh & The Resilient

  • Soreth is their nightmare—proof bearing Entropy corrupts absolutely
  • Their rotation now defined by not becoming Soreth
  • Often say: "Kill me before I turn."
  • Kadesh especially haunted (killed Soreth once, thought he'd saved him)
  • Fear: "If Soreth fell, any of us could"

The Other Sarim

  • Pity and horror mixed
  • Split between redemption and elimination
  • Some see Soreth's truth (the system is broken)
  • Some see only the corruption
  • All agree: cannot let them destroy more Anchors
  • Creates paranoia: "Can we trust our own judgment about bearing Entropy?"

Nepheth

  • First to die permanently
  • Strategic target (Nepheth maintained the cycle)
  • Symbolic target (break the system to free it)
  • Personal element (Nepheth rejected Soreth's testimony)
  • Unclear whether Soreth even remembers why they chose Nepheth first
  • May have been corrupted logic: "Kill the maintainer, expose the flaw"

Threat Assessment

Immediate Dangers

  • Leads incursions against Primordial Anchors
  • Converts Entropic into The Absolved (growing army)
  • May infiltrate as ally to gather intelligence
  • Hunts current Sarim (especially The Resilient)
  • Spreads Stage 3 Entropy through Path of Transference
  • Philosophically persuasive (some points are true)

Strategic Threats

  • Former insider: knows all Sarim structures, weaknesses, locations
  • May have knowledge of Anchor destruction techniques
  • Could destroy remaining Anchors, making all Sarim deaths permanent
  • Creates paranoia within Sarim: "If the strongest fell, who's next?"
  • Philosophically dangerous: his critique of the system resonates
  • Time is on his side: every year degrades the system further

Long-term Implications

  • Proof that bearing Entropy permanently corrupts (supports rigidity)
  • Evidence that system itself may be flawed (supports reform)
  • Question: Can preservation coexist with growth?
  • Problem: If he's right about creation vs. corruption, what does that mean for Sarim purpose?
  • Redemptionist/Eliminationist split may tear Sarim apart from within

For Players

Encounter Framework

First Encounter (Possible Deception):

  • May appear as helpful Sarim, aligned with players
  • Offers assistance against common threat
  • Subtle wrongness in behavior, "off" feeling
  • Rhetoric about strength, endurance, broken systems
  • Insight DC 25+ to detect (20+ if familiar with Sarim lore)

Second Encounter (Growing Suspicion):

  • Inconsistencies emerge in knowledge or methods
  • NPCs or other Sarim express concern
  • Players may witness The Absolved in action
  • Pattern of "perfecting" rather than destroying corruption
  • Geometric precision feels wrong for preservation-focused being

Final Confrontation:

  • Still believes they are righteous
  • May offer players philosophical choice: "Join me in breaking a broken system"
  • Commands The Absolved against party
  • Will retreat if fight turns badly (patient, strategic, has long game)
  • May leave prophetic warning: "You'll see. When you bear it long enough, you'll understand."

Player Choices

If Players Discover the Anchor:

  • Destroy it: Permanent death, eliminationist position, pragmatic
  • Guard it: Preserve chance of return, redemptionist position, hopeful
  • Conceal it: Delay the choice, kick can down road, political

If Players Capture the Crown:

  • Return to Ezareth: Enable potential reforging (250 years)
  • Destroy it: Extend reforging to 2,500+ years (near-permanent)
  • Keep it: Wield legendary power, slowly die/transform
  • Hide it: Prevent reforging entirely, deny Sarim the choice

If Players Hear His Rhetoric:

  • He's not entirely wrong about the system being rigid
  • His methods are absolutely monstrous
  • Creates philosophical question: reform vs. rebellion
  • No easy answers—players must decide what they believe

Crown as Item (if recovered):

  • Provides immense power (CR boost, command abilities, create Absolved)
  • Slowly transforms/corrupts wielder (geometric thinking, rigid certainty)
  • Enable Soreth's eventual reforging if returned to Anchor
  • Impossible for most mortals to wield without dying
  • Soreth's Echo may influence wielder
